text.display: Your phone's glass feels solid, but just under it is an invisible grid, listening for your finger. Thin lines of transparent conductor run across in rows, and down in columns, crossing without ever touching. Every crossing is a tiny capacitor. The chip pulses one line at a time, and measures every crossing. Your finger conducts electricity, so it steals a little of that field, and the signal at that crossing drops. The chip finds where the signal dropped, and that is where you touched.
